name: Sellers standard screw threads
description: A standard family of screw threads proposed by William Sellers used a 60-degree thread profile to enable uniform fasteners and simplify production and repair.

impact.note: A standard that made fasteners uniform for American industry, following an earlier British standard, with a few successor standards.

date.label: April 1864
date.basis: ASME gives month and year of presentation.

events.statement: Sellers presented his proposed screw-thread system to the Franklin Institute in Philadelphia.

evidence.supports: Sellers presented his proposed screw-thread system to the Franklin Institute in Philadelphia.

contributions.resource: Proposed thread system presented at the Franklin Institute

evidence.supports: Sellers devised and presented the system.

date.label: by the 1880s
date.basis: ASME says the system was widespread by the 1880s; the end of that decade is a conservative upper bound, not a start date.

events.statement: The system was widespread in the United States by the 1880s and simplified machinery repair.

evidence.supports: The system was widespread in the United States by the 1880s and simplified machinery repair.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest date established for this specific documented case by the sources inspected; it does not establish an invention date or world priority.

caveats: The source is an institutional retrospective, not the 1864 paper; a 60-degree profile alone does not fully specify a thread family.

research.note: Independently checked both the April 1864 presentation and widespread-by-1880s claims in the cited ASME account; the original 1864 paper was not inspected.

measures.subject: Sellers proposed thread profile
measures.conditions: Included angle as stated in ASME retrospective; a thread family has further dimensions.

evidence.supports: Sellers proposed a 60-degree profile in April 1864.
